description: The chart illustrates, for each year from 2012 to 2022, the number of hateful communication datasets categorized as “Untargeted” versus “Targeted,” displayed as stacked bars. The horizontal axis contains the categorical variable “Year,” labeled “Year,” with years ordered chronologically from 2012 through 2022. The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “Number of datasets,” shown on a linear scale from 0 up to 160 with regularly spaced tick marks at 20-unit intervals (0, 20, 40, …, 160). Each year is represented by one stacked bar with a blue lower segment for “Untargeted” and an orange upper segment for “Targeted,” as indicated by the legend titled “Targets” in the upper-left of the plot. Approximate stacked totals and segment sizes by year are: 2012 shows a very small orange-only bar (about 2 targeted, ~0 untargeted); 2013 shows a very small blue-only bar (about 2 untargeted, ~0 targeted); 2014 and 2015 each show very small orange-only bars (about 2 targeted each); 2016 shows a short stack totaling roughly 13 (about 4 untargeted in blue plus about 9 targeted in orange); 2017 totals roughly 28 (about 12 untargeted plus about 16 targeted); 2018 totals roughly 48 (about 20 untargeted plus about 28 targeted); 2019 totals roughly 65 (about 12 untargeted plus about 53 targeted); 2020 totals roughly 130 (about 48 untargeted plus about 82 targeted); 2021 reaches the top end of the scale at roughly 160 (about 66 untargeted plus about 94 targeted); and 2022 shows a shorter stack around the high 30s (about 10 untargeted plus about 27 targeted), with the 2022 bar rendered in noticeably lighter/paler shades than the preceding years. The bars are not sorted by magnitude; they follow chronological order, and no numeric annotations are shown on the bars.
